podcast.title: Collaboration with Travis Barker
podcast.body: For her 2021 album, Willow collaborated with Travis Barker of Blink-182 to infuse a pop-punk sound into her music. "she switched things up a bit into a more pop punk vein with help from Travis Barker of Blink 182."

podcast.title: Early Pop Success
podcast.body: At the age of 10, Willow achieved significant pop success with her single "Whip My Hair," which became a top 15 hit. "At age 10, she released a single called With My Hair, which became a top 15 pop hit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Genre Exploration
podcast.body: Willow has explored several different styles and genres throughout her musical career, ultimately finding a particular talent and comfort in punk pop. "She's gone through several different styles in genres. But really seems to have a flair for punk pop, working on her own as well as collaborating with people like Machine Gun Kelly and Travis Barker of Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Parents' Musical Background
podcast.body: Willow is the daughter of Will Smith, a rapper, and Jada Pinkett Smith, who is a singer for the new metal band Wicked Wisdom, indicating a strong musical lineage. "She's the daughter of Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith, two people have had their own music careers. Will is a rapper, of course, and mom is a singer of a new metal band called Wicked Wisdom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transition from Acting to Music
podcast.body: Willow initially achieved significant success as an actor, winning multiple awards, before finding her true passion and home in the world of music. "Willow started out as an actor and did really, really well winning a bunch of awards. But she really found a home in the world of music."

xref.title: Prolific Collaborator and Producer (2015-2022)
xref.body: Over a seven-year period, Travis Barker became a highly active collaborator and producer, appearing on numerous records. His extensive list of collaborations includes artists such as Young Blood, The Game, M&M, Stevie O'Kee, LL Cool J, Pitbull, Lights, Kenny Hoopla, Machine Gun Kelly, Halsey, Willow Smith, and Dirty Heads. "Travis Barker seemed willing to collaborate and produce just about anyone, and he would appear in a ton of records over the next seven years."

xref.title: Alleged Spreading of Ashes
xref.body: Courtney Love allegedly spread some of Kurt Cobain's ashes in 1994 at the base of a large cedar tree in Tiny Veretta Park, which is situated next door to their former Seattle residence. She also ensured that some of his ashes remained under a willow tree on the property of their last home, securing a contractual right to access and remove that tree later if she wished. "Beside the benches is a huge cedar at the base of which is where Courtney allegedly spread some of Kurt's ashes in 1994."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ashes at Veretta Park and Willow Tree
xref.body: Following Kurt Cobain's death in 1994, some of his ashes were allegedly spread by Courtney Love at the base of a huge cedar tree in Tiny Veretta Park, which is adjacent to his last home. Additionally, some of his ashes are confirmed to be beneath a willow tree located within the property of his former house. When Courtney Love sold the house, she included a contractual clause stipulating her right to return and remove that specific willow tree to replant it elsewhere. "Beside the benches is a huge cedar at the base of which is where Courtney allegedly spread some of Kurt's ashes in 1994."

xref.title: Diverse Fanbase
xref.body: Her fanbase is wide-ranging, including prominent figures like Billie Eilish, Ed Sheeran, Charlie XCX, Willow Smith, and Olivia Rodrigo. Even Rob Halford of the metal band Judas Priest openly expresses his admiration for Avril Lavigne. "Fans include Billy Eilish, Ed Sheeran, Charlie XCX, Willow Smith and Olivia Rodrigo, even Rob Hulford of Judas Priest says he's a fan of Avril Lavigne."

xref.title: Management of Kurt Cobain's Last House
xref.body: Following Kurt Cobain's death in 1994, his wife, Courtney Love, had the greenhouse where his body was found torn down in 1996. A year later, in 1997, she sold the 171 Lake Washington Boulevard East property to a Japanese businessman. When selling the house, Love included a unique clause in the contract, granting her the right to return at any time to remove a willow tree on the property, under which some of Kurt Cobain's ashes were located, and replant it elsewhere. "Courtney had the greenhouse where Kurt's body was found in 1994, torn down in 1996."
